entities.summary:
Aimo of Toul was the second recorded bishop of Toul, a Roman Catholic saint venerated in the region of Lorraine, France. He is believed to have been born around 300 AD and died sometime after 378 AD. The exact circumstances of his life are unknown, but he is known for his piety and his efforts to spread Christianity throughout the region.

Aimo's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he played a significant role in the development of Christian worship and liturgy in the early centuries of Christianity. His teachings and writings have been preserved through the ages, providing valuable insights into the spiritual practices of the early Church.

Despite the passing of centuries, Aimo's significance remains palpable in the modern era. His devotion to his faith and his commitment to spreading its message continue to inspire believers around the world.

The impact of Aimo's life can be seen in the many churches and shrines dedicated to him throughout Europe, including the magnificent Basilica of Saint-Aignan in Normandy, France. This magnificent structure, built in the 12th century, is a testament to the enduring power of faith and the legacy of this remarkable saint.
